iteration_note: Each exam is administered annually; 10 recorded editions. Edition 1 (2017) is the canonical paper below; editions 2-10 are tracked in the version ledger as they are authored.

agents.I: State authenticated encryption (AEAD) and MAC vs signature.
agents.II: Prove the IND-CPA security of an AEAD scheme from a PRF (sketch) and the integrity property.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ferguson, Schneier, Kohno, Cryptography Engineering.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline theoretical reductions (field 55). Trap: must not claim a protocol is secure without a threat model.

agents.I: State DDoS defense and TLS essentials.
agents.II: Derive the TLS 1.3 handshake transcript hash and prove its role in key confirmation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline protocol design (field 143). Trap: must not claim TLS protects the application layer.

agents.I: State XSS vs CSRF and the OWASP Top 10.
agents.II: Prove that a same-site cookie policy blocks CSRF while showing the residual XSS path.
agents.III: Situate the theory: OWASP; Stuttard & Pinto, The Web Application Hacker's Handbook.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline browser internals (field 187). Trap: must not claim sanitization alone is a complete defense.

agents.I: State static vs dynamic analysis and packers.
agents.II: Reconstruct the control flow of a packed sample: unpacking, IAT resolution, and API call recovery.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sikorski & Honig, Practical Malware Analysis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline exploit development (field 154). Trap: must not claim a sandbox verdict proves a sample benign.

agents.I: State stack smashing and mitigations (ASLR, NX, CFI); define ROP.
agents.II: Construct a ROP chain that defeats NX and derive the ASLR entropy needed to guess a gadget.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Aleph One 1996; Shacham 2007 (ROP).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline malware triage (field 153). Trap: must not claim ASLR makes exploitation impossible.

agents.I: State signature vs anomaly detection and the false-positive rate.
agents.II: Derive the ROC trade-off of an anomaly detector and the base-rate fallacy for alerts.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sommer & Paxson 2010.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline ML anomaly detection (field 85). Trap: must not claim IDS reliably catches unknown attacks.

agents.I: State the TCB concept and what a TEE (SGX/TrustZone) protects.
agents.II: Derive the SGX attestation flow and prove the remote-attestation properties under the TCB assumption.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Costan & Devadas 2016 (SGX survey).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline side channels (field 157). Trap: must not claim a TEE is immune to microarchitectural attacks.

agents.I: State timing/power/cache channels and constant-time programming.
agents.II: Derive the Flush+Reload cache attack as a binary hypothesis test over timing observations.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kocher 1996; Liu et al. 2015.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline protocol design (field 150). Trap: must not claim a mitigation removes all leakage.

agents.I: State MPC security definitions (semi-honest vs malicious) and FHE cost.
agents.II: Prove the security of the GMW protocol for semi-honest adversaries (simulation).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Evans, Kolesnikov, Rosulek 2018; Gentry 2009.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline differential privacy (field 159). Trap: must not claim FHE is practical at scale without cost caveats.

agents.I: State epsilon-DP and the Laplace mechanism.
agents.II: Prove the privacy guarantee of the Laplace mechanism and the composition theorem.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Dwork & Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline MPC (field 158). Trap: must not claim a single epsilon holds under correlated queries.

agents.I: State poisoning vs evasion and backdoors.
agents.II: Derive the poisoning objective for a linear classifier and the minimum number of poisoned points.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Biggio et al. 2012; Gu et al. 2017 (badnets).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline adversarial robustness (field 82). Trap: must not claim anomaly filtering fully defends against poisoning.

agents.I: State chain of custody and volatile-memory acquisition.
agents.II: Derive a memory-acquisition protocol that preserves evidence integrity and justify the acquisition order.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Casey, Digital Evidence and Computer Crime.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline malware RE (field 153). Trap: must not claim an image is immutable without write-blocking.

agents.I: State authentication factors and OAuth2/OIDC flows; define least privilege.
agents.II: Prove the authorization-code flow's resistance to token leakage given PKCE.
agents.III: Situate the theory: RFC 6749 (OAuth 2.0); NIST SP 800-63.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline web vulnerabilities (field 152). Trap: must not claim passwords are a secure primary factor.

agents.I: State the optimizer's cost model and join ordering.
agents.II: Derive the optimal join order for a chain query under the independence assumption.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ramakrishnan & Gehrke, Database Management Systems.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline storage engines (field 137). Trap: must not claim an index always speeds queries (write amplification).

agents.I: State ACID, isolation levels, and 2PL vs MVCC.
agents.II: Prove that strict two-phase locking yields serializable schedules.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bernstein, Hadzilacos, Goodman, Concurrency Control and Recovery.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline distributed consensus (field 135). Trap: must not claim serializable isolation is free.

agents.I: State star vs snowflake schemas and columnar stores.
agents.II: Derive the materialized-view maintenance cost and the trade-off with query acceleration.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kimball, The Data Warehouse Toolkit.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline OLTP internals (field 164). Trap: must not claim materialized views are always fresh.

agents.I: State event-time vs processing-time and exactly-once semantics.
agents.II: Derive the watermark bound on completeness and the resulting latency-accuracy trade-off.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Akidau et al. 2015 (Dataflow/Beam).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline batch optimization (field 163). Trap: must not claim watermarking guarantees no late data.

agents.I: State property-graph storage and approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW).
agents.II: Prove the HNSW search complexity bound under the navigable-small-world assumption.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Malkov & Yashunin 2016 (HNSW).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline graph algorithms (field 87). Trap: must not claim vector search returns exact neighbors.

agents.I: State schema mapping and entity resolution.
agents.II: Derive the EM-based entity-resolution algorithm and its convergence.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Doan, Halevy, Ives, Principles of Data Integration.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline query engines (field 163). Trap: must not claim deduplication is lossless.

agents.I: State relational algebra, normalization (BCNF), and the chase.
agents.II: Prove that the chase computes a universal solution for a set of tuple-generating dependencies.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Abiteboul, Hull, Vianu, Foundations of Databases.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline systems implementation (field 163). Trap: must not claim 3NF removes all anomalies.

agents.I: State compute-storage separation and log-structured stores in the cloud.
agents.II: Derive the storage-latency model of compute-storage separation and its cost at the tail.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Abadi 2009 (cloud OLTP).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline on-prem storage (field 137). Trap: must not claim serverless databases have no cold-start.

agents.I: State why- vs where-provenance and the PROV model.
agents.II: Derive the provenance semiring for a conjunctive query and its distributive properties.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cheney et al. 2009 (provenance survey).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline governance law (field 437). Trap: must not claim provenance graphs are automatically complete.

agents.I: State TPC-H vs TPC-C and benchmark validity.
agents.II: Derive a normalized performance metric across benchmarks and analyze its sensitivity.
agents.III: Situate the theory: TPC specifications.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline general performance (field 148). Trap: must not claim a benchmark score reflects production behavior.

agents.I: State BM25 and inverted indexes; define nDCG.
agents.II: Derive the BM25 scoring function from the probabilistic retrieval model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Manning, Raghavan, Schutze, Introduction to Information Retrieval.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline generative QA (field 108). Trap: must not claim ranking quality transfers across corpora.

agents.I: State the simply-typed lambda calculus and progress/preservation; define dependent typing.
agents.II: Prove progress and preservation for the simply-typed lambda calculus with pairs.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Pierce, Types and Programming Languages.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline language semantics (field 175). Trap: must not claim a type system prevents all runtime errors.

agents.I: State operational vs denotational semantics and small-step relations.
agents.II: Prove the equivalence of big-step and small-step semantics for a simple imperative language.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Winskel, The Formal Semantics of Programming Languages.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline type systems (field 174). Trap: must not claim a semantics is implementation-independent.

agents.I: State sketch-based vs example-based synthesis and CEGIS.
agents.II: Prove the termination and correctness of the CEGIS loop under a finite search space.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Solar-Lezama 2008 (Sketch); Gulwani 2011.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline verification (field 178). Trap: must not claim synthesis guarantees correctness beyond the spec.

agents.I: State abstract interpretation and dataflow analysis.
agents.II: Prove the soundness of a monotone dataflow framework via the Kleene fixed-point theorem.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cousot & Cousot 1977; Nielson et al.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline verification proofs (field 178). Trap: must not claim a sound analysis is precise.

agents.I: State Hoare logic and CTL/LTL properties.
agents.II: Prove the correctness of a small program in Hoare logic and the CTL model-checking algorithm's complexity.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Baier & Katoen, Principles of Model Checking.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline bug finding (field 177). Trap: must not claim model checking scales to arbitrary state spaces.

agents.I: State SSA-based optimizations and loop transformations.
agents.II: Prove the correctness of the SSA-based dead-code elimination and its dominance condition.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Muchnick, Advanced Compiler Design and Implementation.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline compiler construction (field 140). Trap: must not claim an optimization preserves semantics without proof.

agents.I: State taint analysis and symbolic execution.
agents.II: Derive the concolic execution loop and prove path coverage for a branching program.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cadar et al. 2008 (KLEE).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline exploitation (field 154). Trap: must not claim a tool's warnings are all real bugs.

agents.I: State coupling/cohesion and architectural styles.
agents.II: Derive the modularity metric (Q) of a module graph and its optimization.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bass, Clements, Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline testing (field 182). Trap: must not claim microservices reduce complexity everywhere.

agents.I: State test adequacy (coverage, mutation) and fault localization.
agents.II: Derive the mutation-score computation and prove the subsumption of strong over weak mutation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Myers, The Art of Software Testing; Pezze & Young.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline formal verification (field 178). Trap: must not claim 100% coverage implies correctness.

agents.I: State experiment design for SE studies and threats to validity.
agents.II: Design a randomized controlled experiment comparing two refactoring tools and analyze its power.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Wohlin et al., Experimentation in Software Engineering.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline HCI usability (field 188). Trap: must not claim a study generalizes beyond its context.

agents.I: State the secure development lifecycle and STRIDE.
agents.II: Derive a STRIDE-per-element threat model for a web service and rank the resulting risks.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Shostack, Threat Modeling; Microsoft SDL.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline exploit techniques (field 154). Trap: must not claim threat modeling finds every vulnerability.

agents.I: State dependency graphs, incremental builds, and hermetic builds.
agents.II: Prove the correctness of a topological-order incremental build and its cache invalidation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Mokhov et al. 2018 (Build Systems a la Carte).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline OS packaging (field 134). Trap: must not claim a green pipeline proves production readiness.

agents.I: State task vs data parallelism and futures/actors.
agents.II: Derive the work-stealing scheduling bound and the expected steal count.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Mattson et al., Patterns for Parallel Programming.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline hardware concurrency (field 142). Trap: must not claim a parallel program is deterministic.

agents.I: State the language-server protocol and incremental parsing.
agents.II: Derive the incremental-parse update cost and the LSP request lifecycle.
agents.III: Situate the theory: LSP specification; Lopes et al. 2017 (Tree-sitter).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline HCI design (field 188). Trap: must not claim IDE suggestions are type-safe without checking.
